Ka Bishar Bniah

Na u Chaucer (1340-1400), ha ri England, la 
shim por ar spah snem ei ei hadien ban kha ia ka 
bishar bniah (criticism). Kata ka jia tad haduh 
ki snem 1575-1600. ka aiom balung jong u 
Stephen Gosson bad U Philip Sidney Ngam mut 
pat ban kyntiew skong la la ka jong. Ha ka thoh 
ka tar khasi, naduh ka por u Thomas Jones, 
mynba u la seng nongnm la ka, la shim por tang 
kumba 60 snem hadien ban kha la kajmgbishar 
bniah (criticism)

Ka bishar bniah, ha ka thoh ka tar Khasi, 
kumba ka paw, ka mih ka kyrsoi na ka kynja

Ki ar tylli ki phew snem ba nyngkong jong ka

ka aiom bet symbai jong ka juk thymmai - ka 
juk jong ka bishar bniah ha ka ktien bad ka thoh 
ka tar Khasi.

Ha nga hi, ka criticism ka dei ka lynti bah 
sha ka jingkhraw jong ki nongthoh bad ki

THE GIANT WHEEL

Ah! Man of the march, peeks riding the life’s cart; 
Humming and singing, as the wheels are ringing. 
And life is joyous, and the tune melodious; 
And life is a thrill, fast moving as a reel; 
Tingling like a hymn, with rhyming and rhythm. 
One stop, another, and the load is heavier; 
Seeing the Winter, and the last, is so near;

And life is drooping, as the storm is blowing; 
Ever, he struggles, and braving the hurdles; 
Good path is to learn, righteousness is to earn; 
There comes to an end, and the place is Heaven.
